title: Do you test your game on both AMD and NVIDIA?
author: Limp_Bus3865
selftext: I never published a game, and I am developing it on NVIDIA. Do you develop on two machines, one AMD other NVIDIA, to avoid graphics quirks, or do you just publish the game and fix the glitches once the players report it? and if so, how do you fix it if you don't have their hardware?

comments.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
comments.body: Test on Intel. If it's good there, its good everywhere.

replies.author: Limp_Bus3865
replies.body: nvidia is a little bit more lenient and allows much more quirks to pass than amd, that is what I am worried about

comments.author: midasHanduly
comments.body: it happened that i have a full amd system and my friend is on nvidia gpu. So far no quirks, bugs or anything that could have affected the visuals or gameplay in any shape or form. We even tested the game on a mac, and apart from a separate build and some performance issues (which couldve been the hardware issue) there were literally 0 issues. Therefore, i dont think u should even think about it, unless you are implementing hardware specific technologies like fsr, dlss framegen etc.

replies.author: Limp_Bus3865
replies.body: Thanks for giving me a peace of mind. Yeah, I think if you are developing games in existing game engines, they usually don't have a lot of differences between the two providers, and if they do like Godot, these differences are known and avoidable. But I built my own engine for a really resource intensive games and now I am worried about it running on AMD. But I will try it on an integrated AMD GPU inside of CPU, this will catch some quirks at least.

replies.author: midasHanduly
replies.body: i think its gonna work, i see no reason for it not to
